content:
Alex: RFC follow-up: role vs intent model for svc->svc auth. After today's design review a few concrete tradeoffs came up around runtime cost, migration pain, and observability. want a short sync on a pragmatic path forward.
Maria: +1. core tradeoff: roles = cheap checks (role_id -> allow/deny), intents = richer semantics (why call, caller goal) but imply extra claims evaluation or a policy engine hit.
Sam: can we do a hybrid? have stable role checks for the common fast path, and require an explicit intent assertion for sensitive routes (e.g., billing write, key material ops).
Jin: hybrid is pragmatic, but need a deterministic mapping and a migration plan. otherwise ops will see inconsistent behavior when services start emitting intents.
Carol: also think about telemetry: if we synthesize intents from roles (role->intent derivation) we lose caller intent signal unless we emit a derived_intent tag on traces.
Alex: proposal sketch: 1) default path = role_id check from cache (redis/fast lookup). 2) optional "intent assertion" claim (JWT-style, short-lived) included by caller when calling sensitive endpoints. 3) endpoint config: required_intents = [] or null. If required_intents present, server must validate assertion and check allowed intent.
Maria: whats the shape of the assertion? minimal example: a short-lived JWT signed by caller's key with claim `intent` and `exp`. we should document verification: server verifies signature, checks exp, matches caller principal == sub.
Sam: implementation note: prefer separate header (X-Intent-Assertion) so normal paths dont parse it. verify using cached public keys (rotate on KMS event). keep verification cheap: cache jwk sets per principal with TTL.
Jin: avoid a DB round-trip per request. caching public keys + caching verified assertions for microseconds-level reuse (nonce+exp) helps. also rate-limit verification fallback to protect CA.
Carol: security nit: include `nonce` or `jti` to limit replay, and require `exp` fairly short (e.g., 30s). also consider binding to transport (mTLS cert hash) if available.
Alex: example intent JWT payload (pseudocode):
```
{
  "sub": "service-a",
  "intent": "artifact:publish",
  "aud": "artifact-service",
  "exp": 1710000000,
  "jti": "uuid-v4"
}
```
Server verifies signature, checks `aud` matches endpoint, then either allows based on intent -> policy or falls back to role check if endpoint permits.
Maria: how does this integrate with our RBAC policy language? my thought: add `required_intents` optional field on route policy. policy evaluation order: 1) if required_intents present, require valid intent assertion matching one of them. 2) else evaluate role grants as today. This keeps most routes unchanged.
Sam: fallback semantics: we should allow a mode flag per route: `intent_enforced: strict|permissive`. permissive = accept role if assertion missing; strict = deny unless assertion present. helps staged rollouts.
Jin: rollout checklist (ops): 1) add intent header acceptance in gateway + lightweight verifier 2) deploy policy schema change with permissive mode by default 3) instrument metrics (`intent_present`, `intent_verified`, `intent_mismatch`) 4) flip high-risk routes to strict in canary 5) rotate clients to emit assertions.
Carol: observability: add trace tag `derived_intent` when we map role->intent server-side, and `intent_assertion` when caller supplied one. increment sample logs for failures with minimal PII.
Alex: action items: Maria write policy schema PR (owner: Maria). Sam prototype gateway header & jwk cache (owner: Sam). Jin write rollout playbook & metric names (owner: Jin). Carol add tracing fields to trace spec (owner: Carol). i'll draft a one-pager for security review with attack models.
auth-bot: scheduled: security-review required for intent-assertion flow. please add review request in #eng-security.
Alex: thanks everyone. if no objections i'll file the small RFC update and start the prototype next week.
